name: @forestrie/mcp-verify

tools.name: verify_receipt
tools.description: Verify a Forestrie receipt against the EXACT registered payload bytes and an entry id, at a trust root you choose. Mirrors `forestrie verify`. Offline: no network, no key, no account. Returns both the mechanical stages and the four trust questions. KS256 contract roots take an optional ks256Attestation (fetched elsewhere; this tool never calls the chain).

oneOf.description: Trust a log owner key you obtained out of band: a 64-byte P-256 key (keyXy) or a 20-byte KS256 address (ks256Address). Same questions as genesis; the key-to-log binding is ASSERTED by you, not proven — an address in particular proves nothing about which log it owns. A contract (Safe) address needs ks256Attestation on the tool call to verify offline.

oneOf.description: Fold a retained checkpoint chain and match any authenticated link. Answers split-view. Needs genesis or keyXy to root the first link. Each link's delegation certificate limits are enforced: a link signed beyond the certificate's mmrEnd fails delegation_out_of_range, and a link covering the receipt's leaf signed under a certificate that had expired when the leaf was sequenced fails delegation_expired (never wall-clock). A KS256 contract (Safe) genesis root takes ks256Attestation on the tool call.

trust.description: Which anchor you are willing to trust

path.description: filesystem path, read by the stdio adapter

ks256Attestation.description: ERC-1271 attestation artifact (encodeKs256Attestation CBOR) for a KS256 CONTRACT root. Fetched elsewhere — this server never touches the network: use mcp-resolve's `fetch_ks256_attestation` tool or forestrie-cli's `fetch-ks256-attestation`. With it a contract-rooted delegation verifies as valid under the contract's signers at the attested block. Usable with the genesis, known-log-key and checkpoint-chain roots (checkpoint-chain also needs trust.genesis for the forest chain id; one attestation binds one certificate, so links signed under a different certificate still fail). Not with known-accumulator. Trust: the attestation is unsigned and only as good as whoever fetched it; accept one only from a party you would trust to read the chain for you — {b64: <standard base64>} (base64 is accepted as an alias), or {path: <a file the local server reads>}

tools.name: verify_grant_receipt
tools.description: Verify a Forestrie grant receipt against the committed grant (Forestrie-Grant COSE Sign1, or raw grant payload CBOR plus an entry id), at a trust root you choose. Mirrors `forestrie verify-grant`. This is the tool that answers the append-authority question: the leaf IS the grant. KS256 contract roots take an optional ks256Attestation (fetched elsewhere; this tool never calls the chain).

tools.name: decode_receipt
tools.description: Render a COSE receipt's CBOR as JSON — headers, named labels, payload, signature and inclusion proof. NO VERIFICATION is performed: a receipt that decodes cleanly may still be invalid. Mirrors `forestrie decode-receipt --json`.

path.description: filesystem path, read by the stdio adapter

receipt.description: the COSE receipt to render — {b64: <standard base64>} (base64 is accepted as an alias), or {path: <a file the local server reads>}

tools.name: verify_self
tools.description: Verify this package's own release-time self-registration receipt: does the receipt commit the signed statement, does that statement's payload match the bundled provenance.json byte-for-byte, and does its ES256 signature verify under the bundled log owner key? No inputs required. Defaults to the known-log-key root with the bundled key, not genesis — the publications log is a grandchild of the forest root and nothing walks that grant chain yet (docs/self-registration.md). Errors clearly, rather than throwing, when this checkout has no fixtures/self/ bundle (any checkout that is not itself the published tarball).

oneOf.description: the default: the bundled log owner key, fixtures/self/log-key.xy.b64

the bundled forest genesis document. Reports delegation_invalid for this receipt today: the publications log is a grandchild of the forest root and nothing walks the grant chain that far yet (docs/self-registration.md).

instructions: Offline Forestrie receipt verification. Every tool is pure over bytes: no network, no account, no key, no backend. Choose a trust root deliberately — the answer tells you which of the four trust questions that root can answer, and 'not_answered_by_this_root' is a real answer that must be shown to the user. KS256 (secp256k1) roots verify offline: an EOA root by ecrecover, a contract root (Safe) only with a ks256Attestation — an ERC-1271 record fetched elsewhere (mcp-resolve's fetch_ks256_attestation, or forestrie-cli's fetch-ks256-attestation), never by this server. A contract root is then valid under the contract's signers at the attested block, a narrower guarantee; the result's ks256Attestation names that block.
